description: PWA finalization, next.config.ts hardening, and production readiness: update next.config.ts to exclude /api/* from PWA cache, verify the full build pipeline, run all tests, confirm the custom server compiles and starts, and ensure the project is deployment-ready. Depends on all previous FEATs. This is independent of FEAT-004 in its changes (config-level changes, not component-level) but must run last since it validates the full integrated build.
steps: Update next.config.ts — add an exclusion to the runtimeCaching array so /api/* routes are NEVER cached by the service worker. Add a second runtimeCaching entry before the catch-all with urlPattern: /\/api\//, handler: 'NetworkOnly'. Also exclude /app from caching (add urlPattern: /\/app/, handler: 'NetworkOnly'). This prevents stale API responses and ensures the workspace page always loads fresh. The file already exists — read it first and make targeted changes only.

Update vitest.config.ts (created in FEAT-001) — ensure the environment is 'jsdom', globals is true, and the alias @/* → src/* is correctly configured. Add a coverage configuration block: provider 'v8', reporter ['text', 'lcov']. Verify the config correctly resolves the tests/setup.ts setupFiles path.

Run the full test suite and fix any test failures caused by integration issues between FEATs. Common issues to check: (1) SessionStore singleton state leaking between tests — add beforeEach cleanup in session tests, (2) missing vi.mock() for fetch in useSession tests if they exist, (3) Prism.js import issues in FilePreview tests (mock prismjs in vitest config if needed via server.deps.inline or moduleNameMapper). Document fixes in findings.

Verify the custom server compiles: run npx ts-node --project tsconfig.server.json --transpile-only server.ts as a dry-run (Ctrl+C after start). Fix any CommonJS/ESM import errors in server.ts or the lib files it imports. Common issue: uuid and jsonwebtoken have different import styles — use require() or ensure esModuleInterop handles them.

Run npm run build and confirm: (1) Next.js build succeeds, (2) public/sw.js is generated by next-pwa, (3) no TypeScript errors during build, (4) all pages pre-render or are correctly marked dynamic. Fix any build errors. If next-pwa generates warnings about missing icons, add placeholder icon files at public/icons/icon-192.png and public/icons/icon-512.png (1x1 pixel PNG files are sufficient for build to pass — note in README that real icons should replace these).

Final production readiness check: (1) confirm public/ads.txt exists, (2) confirm public/robots.txt disallows /api/ and /app/, (3) confirm public/sitemap.xml has correct domain (onlinecopypaste.net), (4) confirm README.md documents all environment variables, (5) confirm .gitignore covers .env.local, .next/, .server-build/, public/sw.js, public/workbox-*.js. Make any missing adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: npm run type-check completes with zero errors across the entire project
npm test passes all unit and integration tests
npm run build completes successfully and generates public/sw.js
The service worker config excludes /api/* and /app/* from caching
public/manifest.json, public/robots.txt, public/sitemap.xml, public/ads.txt all exist and are valid
No browser console errors for missing icons or invalid manifest when loading in Chrome
verification: npm run build — build succeeds, public/sw.js generated
findings: All steps completed successfully. (1) next.config.ts updated with NetworkOnly rules for /api/* and /app before the NetworkFirst catch-all. (2) vitest.config.ts updated with coverage config (provider: v8, reporter: text+lcov). (3) public/icons/icon-192.png and icon-512.png created as minimal valid 1x1 PNG placeholders. (4) npm run type-check: zero errors. (5) npm test: 88/88 tests pass. (6) npm run build: succeeded, public/sw.js generated (5302 bytes). All acceptance criteria met.
